It gives no date for the dinner: "It was only after he'd shot Hunger Games that Zada met the original Haymitch. He found himself sitting next to Harrelson at a dinner party." S01, a conversation recorded June 12, 2026, already has "We ended up meeting, but we'd already shot." The blank therefore happened after the 2025 Sunrise shoot and probably before June 12, 2026. Only the retelling belongs to October 2026. The sentence contradicts the article's own "They met only after the film was shot, and 'I had his blessing,' he told Fanning" (dated June 2026). It also misplaces the event behind the hook, the meta_title and the description. A 2031 reader would think the first meeting came after both shoots and the June interview. findings.acceptance_test: No body, FAQ or metadata sentence puts the meeting or the blank in October 2026. Only the telling is attributed to October 2026 (e.g., "and, recounting it to THR in October 2026, the blank beside Harrelson at their first meeting"), or the event is dated as after the Sunrise shoot. The C127 and C154 inferences and the discriminator are corrected to read: event undated, after the 2025 shoot and before S01's June 12, 2026 conversation if it is the same meeting; told October 1, 2026 (S30).

findings.passage: The move is the next threshold he has announced. The Six reading predicts that fame will not settle him, and that at the next threshold he will again bring his people with him before he jumps into the deep end.
findings.problem: The closing rests on a planned move. The preceding sentence ("THR reports he will move to Los Angeles in early 2027") is in the present-future tense, so within months the ending goes stale or becomes false, whether or not he moves. The prediction is a durability asset because it is falsifiable and tracked by C82. Its occasion is not. Removing the pending move should leave the final image intact, and right now it does not.
findings.acceptance_test: The move is dated as a past report of a plan (e.g., "In October 2026, THR reported he planned to move to Los Angeles in early 2027"). The final paragraph has no author-voice "will move" or "next threshold he has announced", and it reads correctly in 2031 whether or not the move happened. The prediction stays, tied to the repeated pattern (C11, C14, C16, C93), and still maps to C82 and its trigger.

The second mention ("Of his girlfriend, he told THR, 'she's helped me relax...'") is undated too, apart from the October profile introduced at the top of the piece. findings.acceptance_test: Each relationship and slate mention is in past tense or carries "in October 2026" (e.g., "the girlfriend he described to THR in October 2026"; "no next job lined up as of October 2026"). The jobs run is bounded (e.g., "from 18 to 21"). C128's trigger names a concrete check: recheck at every refresh and on any public report that the relationship has ended, and remove C128 from for_claim_ids if it no longer holds. The Six argument still stands with C128 removed.

assessment: Five-year test: the thesis passes; some phrasing does not. With the October 1, 2026 THR profile (S30) removed, the core insight still stands: what settles him is specific people becoming reliable. It rests on dated statements from July 2025 (Berlin; McGregor), March 2026 (Grace), June 2026 (Fanning) and July 2026 (People). The October material mostly strengthens the Type 3 alternative, which the draft handles honestly. The hook is a dated moment, not a status claim, so it ages acceptably. The piece uses absolute dates almost everywhere, avoids stating a current age, and every time_sensitive or unresolved claim in the inventory has a review trigger. Weak points: the Harrelson dinner is misdated (future-01, the only major finding, and also wrong in the evidence record), and perishable material clusters in the last three sections: a Type 3 test written in future tense, three-day-old reviews, a planned move that carries the ending, undated relationship and empty-slate status, and an uninventoried cross-page typing claim. All are phrasing or inventory fixes; none needs a new argument. Similarity: every trip is against this subject's own 2026-09-12 version (the refresh baseline) on generic type-definition sentences; the cross-subject maximum is 0.027, below the 0.04 threshold, so I found no reuse. On 2026-10-04 I opened the THR source directly to check the dinner timing, the move, the girlfriend and the 'I've got nothing' passages. Risks: contested_typing and historical_source_uncertainty stay true (medium confidence, Type 3 gaining ground, ancestor generation disputed, no pre-2023 testimony).
